q: What does Paul always remember before God concerning the Thessalonians?
a: Paul remembers their work of faith, their labor of love, and their patience of hope.

q: In what four ways did the gospel come to the Thessalonians?
a: The gospel came to the Thessalonians in word, in power, in the Holy Spirit, and in much assurance.

q: What was happening to the Thessalonians as they received the word of the gospel?
a: The Thessalonians received the word in much hardship.

q: What was the Thessalonians’ attitude as they received the word of the gospel?
a: The Thessalonians received the word with joy in the Holy Spirit.

q: What happened to the word of the Lord after the Thessalonians received it?
a: The word of the Lord rang out in every place their faith went out.

q: What were the Thessalonians worshiping before they became believers in the true God?
a: The Thessalonians were worshiping idols before they became believers in the true God.

q: For what were Paul and the Thessalonians waiting?
a: Paul and the Thessalonians were waiting for Jesus to come from heaven.

q: From what does Jesus deliver us?
a: Jesus delivers us from the wrath to come.

q: How had Paul and his companions been treated before coming to the Thessalonians?
a: Paul and his companions had suffered and had been treated shamefully.

q: Who is Paul desiring to please with his preaching of the gospel?
a: Paul is desiring to please God with his preaching of the gospel.

q: What did Paul not do in his preaching of the gospel?
a: Paul did not use flattery, nor seek glory from people.

q: How did Paul treat the Thessalonians when he was among them?
a: Paul was gentle with the Thessalonians, like a mother or father with their own children.

q: What did Paul and his companions do so that they were not a burden to the Thessalonians?
a: Paul and his companions worked night and day so that they were not a burden to the Thessalonians.

q: How did Paul treat the Thessalonians when he was among them?
a: Paul was gentle with the Thessalonians like a mother or father with their own children.

q: How did Paul tell the Thessalonians they should walk?
a: Paul told the Thessalonians that they should walk in a manner worthy of God who calls them to his own kingdom and glory.

q: As what kind of word did the Thessalonians receive the message Paul preached to them?
a: The Thessalonians received the message as the word of God, not as the word of man.

q: What had the unbelieving Jews done which did not please God?
a: The unbelieving Jews persecuted the churches in Judea, killed Jesus and the prophets, drove out Paul, and forbade Paul to speak to the Gentiles.

q: Why was Paul not able to come to the Thessalonians even though that was his wish?
a: Paul was not able to come because Satan hindered him.

q: What will the Thessalonians be for Paul at the Lord’s coming?
a: The Thessalonians will be Paul’s hope, joy, and crown of glorying at the Lord’s coming.

q: What did Paul do, even though he would be left behind in Athens?
a: Paul sent Timothy to strengthen and comfort the believers in Thessalonica.

q: To what did Paul say he was appointed?
a: Paul said that he was appointed to afflictions.

q: About what was Paul concerned regarding the Thessalonians?
a: Paul was concerned that somehow the tempter had tempted them and that his labor had been in vain.

q: What comforted Paul when Timothy returned from Thessalonica?
a: Paul was comforted to hear the good news of the Thessalonians’ faith and love, and that they longed to see him.

q: Paul says that he lives if the Thessalonians do what?
a: Paul says that he lives if the Thessalonians stand firm in the Lord.

q: For what does Paul pray night and day?
a: Paul prays night and day that he might see the Thessalonians and provide what is lacking in their faith.

q: In what does Paul wish the Thessalonians to increase and abound?
a: Paul wishes the Thessalonians to increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all people.

q: For what event does Paul want the Thessalonians to be prepared by having their hearts blameless in holiness?
a: Paul wants the Thessalonians to be prepared for the coming of the Lord Jesus with all his holy ones.

q: What did Paul want the Thessalonians to do with the instructions he had given them about how they must walk and please God?
a: Paul wanted the Thessalonians to continue to walk and please God, and to do even more.

q: What did Paul say was God’s will for the Thessalonians?
a: Paul said God’s will for the Thessalonians was their sanctification.

q: What do the people need to learn?
a: The people need to learn to control their desires to have sex.

q: What would happen to a brother who sinned in the matter of sexual immorality?
a: The Lord would be an avenger toward a brother who sinned in the matter of sexual immorality.

q: Who does a person reject who rejects the call to holiness?
a: A person who rejects the call to holiness rejects God.

q: What were the Thessalonians doing that Paul wanted them to do even more?
a: Paul wanted the Thessalonians to love one another even more.

q: What were the Thessalonians to do so that they walked properly before unbelievers and had need of nothing?
a: The Thessalonians were to be quiet, mind their own business, and work with their hands.

q: About what subject did the Thessalonians possibly have a misunderstanding?
a: The Thessalonians possibly had a misunderstanding about what happened to those who slept.

q: What will God do for those who have fallen asleep in Jesus?
a: God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Christ.

q: Who will rise first, and then who will rise together with them?
a: The dead in Christ will rise first, then those who are still alive will be caught up with them.

q: How will the Lord descend from heaven?
a: The Lord will descend from heaven with a shout and with the trumpet of God.

q: Who will the risen meet, and for how long?
a: The risen will meet the Lord in the air, and will always then be with the Lord.

q: What did Paul tell the Thessalonians to do with his teaching about those who had fallen asleep?
a: Paul told the Thessalonians to comfort one another with his words.

q: How does Paul say the day of the Lord will come?
a: Paul says the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.

q: What will some people be saying when sudden destruction comes upon them?
a: Some people will be saying, “Peace and safety.”

q: Why does Paul say the day of the Lord should not overtake the believers like a thief?
a: Because the believers are not in darkness, but are sons of the light, the day of the Lord should not overtake them like a thief.

q: What does Paul tell the believers to do regarding the coming day of the Lord?
a: Paul tells the believers to watch and be sober.

q: For what are the believers destined by God?
a: The believers are destined by God for salvation through the Lord Jesus Christ.

q: What attitude does Paul say the believers should have toward those who are over them in the Lord?
a: Paul says that they should acknowledge and highly regard them in love.

q: What does Paul say no one should do when evil is done to them?
a: Paul says that no one should pay back evil when evil is done to them.

q: What does Paul say that the believers should do in everything, and why?
a: Paul says that the believers should give thanks in everything, because this is the will of God for them.

q: What instructions does Paul give the believers about prophecies?
a: Paul instructs the believers to not despise prophecies, and to test all things, holding on to that which is good.

q: What does Paul pray that God will do for the believers?
a: Paul prays that God will sanctify the believers completely in spirit, soul, and body.

q: What does Paul pray would be with the believers?
a: Paul prays that the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ would be with the believers.
